chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafs, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with emancipating a child born of adultery.

key_terms.وَلَدُ الزِّنَا: walad al-zina — a child born of adultery or fornication; in Islamic law the child bears no legal stigma from the parents' sin
key_terms.يُعْتَقَ: yu'taqa — to be freed or emancipated from slavery; the act of manumission (itq)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to free a slave born of adultery?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a permissibility ruling regarding the emancipation of a slave who was born as a result of illicit relations (walad al-zina). The ruling affirms that such a child's circumstances of birth do not preclude the lawfulness of granting them freedom. In Islamic jurisprudence, this addresses a question that would have arisen naturally in a society where slavery was practiced — whether the circumstances of birth affected the legal validity of manumission.
